youtube.title: Counting Coins for Kids! Penny, Nickel, Dime Shop | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
It's the grand opening of Frog's Toy Shop! Meet the penny, nickel and dime, watch the tiny dime win the coin race to 10 cents, and learn to count coins by starting with the dimes. Pig keeps trying to pay with silly things!
For first graders learning US coins. Coins are small: keep them out of mouths and count with a grown-up.

do.text: Welcome to Frog's Toy Shop! Grand opening!
Snip, snip!
Hello! One ball, please. Here's my flower!
Pig, a flower is not money!
Oh! Hee hee.
Let's learn our coins first!
These are US coins. Coins are money.
US coins
This is a penny.
penny
A penny is brown. It is worth 1 cent.
1 cent
Its edge is smooth.
This is a nickel.
nickel
A nickel is silver. It is worth 5 cents.
5 cents
Its edge is smooth too. It's the biggest of the three.
And this is a dime.
dime
A dime is silver. It is worth 10 cents!
10 cents
The dime is the smallest, with tiny ridges on its edge.
Fun fact: the penny has Abraham Lincoln on it.
The nickel has Thomas Jefferson. The dime has Franklin Roosevelt.
Penny?
One cent! Nickel?
Five cents! Dime?
Ten cents! Hold up both hands for a dime!
Silver does not mean more. The nickel is silver too!
Dimes count by ten, nickels by five, pennies by one!
The nickel is the biggest. So it's the best!
Hmm. Let's have a coin race to 10 cents!
Pennies, nickels and the dime. Each hop adds its value.
Which coin will reach 10 cents first?
I bet on the nickels. They're the biggest!
The dime wins in one giant hop! Small but mighty!
small but mighty
Ten pennies, two nickels, one dime. All make 10 cents.
Fun fact: the dime is the smallest US coin.
But a dime is worth more than a penny or a nickel.
Wow! Bigger is not always more.
I have my piggy bank!
Let me count. Pennies first. 1, 2.
Then 5? No, 7? Then 17, 27? Hmm, 12?
Oh no, I'm all mixed up!
Here's the trick. Start with the coin worth the most.
Dimes first, then nickels, then pennies.
dimes first
27 cents! That's much easier.
Ohh, dimes first!
Pig, you try! Count them again, dimes first.
27 cents! I did it!
Dimes count by ten, nickels by five, pennies by one!
I want the ball. It costs 8 cents.
Pig gives 1 nickel and 3 pennies. Count with me!
8 cents! That's right!
Next, the apple. 15 cents. Here's an egg!
An egg? No, Pig! Coins, please!
Pig gives 1 dime and 1 nickel.
15 cents! Thank you!
And the balloon, please. 21 cents.
2 dimes and 1 penny. Count, friends!
21 cents. Ding!
Welcome to my trade table! Fair trades only.
5 pennies make 1 nickel.
2 nickels make 1 dime.
And 10 pennies make 1 dime. All 10 cents!
Let's count the pennies. Count by ones!
10 pennies, 10 cents. The same as 1 dime!
Same amount, different coins.
same amount
Now a big mix. 3 dimes, 2 nickels, 4 pennies.
Dimes first!
44 cents! You counted like a pro.
Shop quiz! Count, then shout the answer.
Shop Quiz
Question one. 2 dimes and 3 pennies. How much?
23 cents!
Question two. How many pennies make one nickel?
5 pennies!
Question three. Which is worth more, a nickel or a dime?
The dime! 10 cents is more than 5.
Question four. 1 dime, 1 nickel, 1 penny. How much?
16 cents!
Last one. Show 12 cents with coins.
1 dime and 2 pennies! 10, 11, 12.
12 pennies work too, or 2 nickels and 2 pennies!
Ding, ding! All correct!
One last thing. The gift, please! 32 cents.
Pig gives 3 dimes and 2 pennies.
Exactly right, Pig!
I paid with real coins this time! Hee hee!
Try a coin rubbing at home, with a grown-up.
Put a coin under paper and rub with a crayon.
Coins are small. Never put them in your mouth!
Closing time!
Penny 1, nickel 5, dime 10. Always count the dimes first!
Bye-bye, shoppers!
